doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: Overdubs and tributes on 'Sacred Hearts'
summary: Layered horns on 'Widow's Walk'; each tune dedicated to someone lost, including 'Country Mike' for Michael Brecker.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You know when you said “overdub” I can’t believe that — I’m going back to it, the “Widow’s Walk,” people have to listen to this because one thing that I remember, especially the first time I heard it was you were playing the melody on the tenor and then the soprano entered. Am I correct? I’m assuming that was you as well. It sounded like then there was an intertwining of two horns and then it ended up in unison.

Yeah it is me. I’m trying to think — yeah the second voice is soprano I’m pretty sure. I don’t think I did it with two tenors. But yeah on that first record there’s another one I did, I did the melody just with three horns. And it’s kind of — I’ve had fun doing that over the years. So “Sacred Hearts,” it didn’t start out originally with it being this kind of tribute album but then it did as the material kind of fell into place. So each song is kind of dedicated to somebody that I lost. Because between the recording of “Sacred Hearts” and the one I did before that which is called “Bohemia” it was like nine or ten years since I did a record under my own name. So “Sacred Hearts” has dedications to all the people that I had lost in those ten years. But it’s not really a sad record, it’s more celebrating them you know. So the one I wrote for Michael Brecker is called “Country Mike.” And at the end there’s a vamp that goes on for a while and there were nine different tracks of me improvising. And that was super fun to put together. And then the orchestrating of it, the melody itself has three or four sopranos playing with the piano and — if you haven’t heard that one I think you would enjoy it, and you can go on YouTube and find that one. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
I’ll check it out. No wonder it took four years.
But I said even on that it’s still — it took nine of me to make one Michael Brecker and not even then was I successful.
